The '''Monroe EPIC''' was a [[programmable calculator]] that came on the market in the 1964. It consisted of a large [[Desktop computer|desktop]] unit which attached to a floor-standing logic tower and was capable of being programmed to perform many computer-like functions. However, the only form of a [[Branch (computer science)|branching instruction]] available was a [[Hard coding|hard-coded]] [[Branch (computer science)|unconditional branch]] (GOTO) that always executed at [[Computer program|program]] completion (the end of the operation [[Stack (abstract data type)|stack]]) to return to the starting instruction of the program (looped back to the beginning of operation stack). This made the creation of [[Conditional (computer programming)|conditional branching logic]], such as IF-THEN-ELSE, impossible.
